- **All three provider types detected**, each with `confidence=0.95`; the negative page reported `0.0`/`not present` — no false positives (also verified on `example.com` and `about:blank`).

assessment.completionStatus: Successful — all 7 task steps completed: captcha plugin installed and loaded, live reCAPTCHA v2 / hCaptcha / Turnstile widgets detected with correct type+siteKey, negative page (Wikipedia) correctly reported isPresent=false, and solver availability (unconfigured) reported via captcha_get_balance.
assessment.successRate: 95% — every requested measurement was obtained; only the optional solving step was unavailable by configuration (no provider key), which is an expected, clearly reported state rather than a failure.
assessment.majorBlockers: None fatal. The only real blocker was that the browser4-captcha plugin is not installed by default and the documented install command (wildcard `*.jar`) fails outright, so installation required reading docs/config.md plus the plugin source to pick the right of 6 JARs. Secondary friction: tool names are invisible in CLI listings and the detect result is an unparseable Kotlin toString.
assessment.mostConfusingAspects: For a first-time user: (1) the capability under test is not present until a plugin install + backend restart, and the documented install command fails; (2) `plugin` output advertises domains (`captcha_get`, `captcha_solve`) that do not exist as tools while hiding `captcha_detect`; (3) `plugin info captcha` 404s with an empty body even though `plugin` prints `plugin captcha`; (4) `tool call` help points at `plugin list`, which lists plugins, not tools; (5) the detection result looks like JSON but its fields live inside a Java toString string, so even `--json` yields nothing directly addressable.
assessment.mostValuableImprovements: Return captcha_detect results as real JSON (a Map, exactly like getBalance already does) — one change removes the need for bespoke parsing in every agent. Then fix plugin discovery end to end: derive the `plugin` listing from tool-spec metadata (real domain + methods), accept the domain name in `plugin info`, and make the documented install command work (single-file validation with an actionable error, or glob/`--latest` support) plus docs naming the version-matched JAR. Lower-effort wins: show the documented `balance`/`providers` keys, unify detector metadata, and document detect latency/wait semantics.

issues.title: Documented `plugin install` wildcard command fails — CLI joins shell-expanded paths into one bogus filename

sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 plugin install browser4-plugins/browser4-captcha/target/browser4-captcha-*.jar   (exactly as written in docs/config.md §CAPTCHA and the `help` Server-plugins footer)
./b4w.ps1 plugin install "a.jar" "b.jar"   (minimal form)
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Installs the intended JAR (or, given 6 versioned JARs, rejects the ambiguity with a message naming the candidates / pointing at a `--latest` / version flag).
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Error: Plugin file not found: browser4-plugins/browser4-captcha/target/browser4-captcha-4.14.0-rc.10.jar browser4-plugins/.../browser4-captcha-4.14.0-rc.5.jar ... browser4-captcha-4.14.1-SNAPSHOT.jar  (exit 1). The CLI reports a single "not found" path built by joining all positional arguments with spaces; there is no hint that 6 files matched or which one is correct.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: handle_plugin_install reads one positional `file` string; the arg parser folds all extra positionals into that same string (space-joined), so a glob expanding to N files becomes one nonexistent path. The error message echoes the joined string, hiding the real cause. Compounding it, browser4-plugins/browser4-captcha/target/ contains 6 JARs (rc.5 … rc.10, 4.14.1-SNAPSHOT) and neither the docs nor the CLI explain which matches the checkout.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:handle_plugin_install() (~line 21839, "Plugin file not found") plus the positional-argument collection feeding it
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Reject more than one positional for `plugin install` with an explicit message ("expected exactly one JAR, got 6 — pick one")
- Or resolve globs inside the CLI and offer `--latest` / `--version <x>` selection, preferring the JAR matching the checked-out version
- Update docs/config.md and the `help` footer to name the version-matched artifact (e.g. `browser4-captcha-<version>.jar`) instead of `*.jar`
- Print the available candidates in the error path so a first-time user can choose without `ls`
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: captcha_detect result is a Java toString() string, not structured JSON — no machine-readable output mode

sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 -s cap tool call captcha_detect
./b4w.ps1 -s cap --json --pretty tool call captcha_detect
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: A structured payload whose fields are directly addressable, e.g. {"isPresent":true,"captchaType":"RECAPTCHA_V2","siteKey":"6Le-...","confidence":0.95,"selector":".g-recaptcha"} — the pattern the same plugin already uses for captcha_get_balance (which returns clean JSON).
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: {"type":"ai.platon.pulsar.captcha.CaptchaDetectionResult","description":"CaptchaDetectionResult(isPresent=true, captchaType=RECAPTCHA_V2, siteKey=6Le-wvkSAAAAAPBMRTvw0Q4Muexq9bi0DJwx_mJ-, action=null, selector=.g-recaptcha, confidence=0.95, metadata={widgetCount=1})"}. Even with the global `--json --pretty` the value stays a string under output.result.description; every consumer must regex-scrape Kotlin data-class syntax, and `metadata` is itself an unquoted map literal.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The tool returns the CaptchaDetectionResult data class; the MCP/agentic result serializer has no JSON mapping for it, so it falls back to toString() wrapped in a type+description envelope. Structured results only survive when the tool returns a plain Map/JSON value (as getBalance does), so the defect is per-return-type, not a protocol limitation.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-plugins/browser4-captcha/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/captcha/CaptchaDetectionResult.kt (serialization) and browser4-plugins/browser4-captcha/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/captcha/tools/CaptchaToolExecutor.kt:callFunctionOn() ("detect" branch)
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Return a Map<String, Any?> from the `detect` branch (same style as getBalance) so the payload is real JSON
- Or register an explicit Jackson serializer for CaptchaDetectionResult in the plugin and honour it in the tool-result layer
- If the toString envelope is intentional, document it and the exact field order in the tool help so parsers are not guesswork
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: `plugin` tool listing shows invented pseudo-domains and never the real tool names

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 plugin
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: A listing a first-time user can act on, e.g. domains with their methods: `captcha` → detect, solve, solve_image, get_balance.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Lists `plugin captcha`, `plugin captcha_get`, `plugin captcha_solve`. The real tools are captcha_detect, captcha_get_balance, captcha_solve, captcha_solve_image: `captcha_detect` never appears, and `captcha_get`/`captcha_solve` look like domains but are artefacts. The only place real method names surface is an error: `plugin captcha bogusMethod` → "Available methods: detect, get_balance, solve, solve_image".
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: available_plugin_domains() strips only the last underscore-separated segment (rsplitn(2,'_')) to derive a domain, so captcha_get_balance → domain captcha_get, captcha_solve_image → captcha_solve. The registration path (CustomToolRegistry / ToolSpec.domain) knows the true domain but is not consulted for the listing.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:available_plugin_domains() (~line 22736) and resolve_plugin_method() (~line 21964)
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Build the listing from the backend's tool-spec metadata (ToolSpec.domain/method) instead of name heuristics
- Print each domain with its methods (and one-line descriptions) so `captcha_detect` is discoverable without invoking a bogus method
- Keep `plugin <domain> <method>` working for multi-word tool names such as captcha_get_balance / captcha_solve_image
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: `plugin info <domain>` fails with a bare 404 and an empty response body

sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 plugin info captcha      # name exactly as printed by `plugin` / `plugin list`
./b4w.ps1 plugin info browser4-captcha   # works
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Either the plugin's details, or an actionable error ("Unknown plugin 'captcha'. Installed plugins: browser4-captcha, browser4-swarm — run `plugin list`").
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Error: HTTP request failed with status 404 Not Found and an empty response body. No indication that the domain/plugin distinction is the problem, and no list of valid names.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The backend's plugin-info lookup is keyed on manifest name / JAR filename only; the CLI passes the user's argument through verbatim and surfaces the empty 404 body. The names the CLI itself advertises elsewhere (`plugin captcha`) are therefore not accepted by its own `info` subcommand.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:handle_plugin_info() (error surfacing) and the backend PluginService info endpoint
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- On 404, retry with a substring/domain match against installed plugin names and say which name was used
- Always return a non-empty error body/help text listing valid manifest names
- Accept the tool-domain alias (`captcha`) as an input form, since that is the vocabulary `plugin` and `tool call` teach
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Per-call latency is dominated by CLI overhead, and detection latency has no documented wait/timeout semantics

sections.body: Time `./b4w.ps1 -s cap tool call captcha_detect` (≈1.7 s) and compare with the backend log line `tool=captcha_detect ... durationMs=3..35`. First detect right after `goto https://accounts.hcaptcha.com/demo` logged durationMs=2542.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Either latency guidance in the docs, or lower per-call overhead — detection itself is effectively instant.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Every detect costs ~1.6–1.8 s wall clock despite 3–35 ms server-side work; `./b4w.ps1 --version` alone costs ~1.2 s (pwsh ~0.3 s + wrapper), so on Windows a 4-page scan spends ~7 s in process/round-trip overhead. The 2.5 s first-detection on the hCaptcha demo shows results also depend on page JS state, and nothing documents whether/when `captcha.detect` waits for lazily rendered widgets (a call made too early could report isPresent=false with no retry hint).
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Two layers: (a) the dev wrapper re-resolves the checkout and spawns PowerShell per command; (b) each tool call performs session resolution round-trips before hitting a ~15 ms backend endpoint. The detectors are single JS evals with no wait loop, so a not-yet-rendered widget is a silent false negative.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: b4w.ps1 (dev wrapper bootstrap), cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs with_session()/call_tool_with_timeout_override(), browser4-plugins/browser4-captcha/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/captcha/detection/ChainedCaptchaDetector.kt
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Document expected detect latency and recommend `batch`/repeated calls where several tool calls are needed in one step
- Document (or add) an optional wait/retry window for lazily rendered widgets, and surface it in the detection result (e.g. `waited: false`)
- Note in docs that per-command CLI overhead on Windows dev wrappers is ~1.2 s and unrelated to plugin performance
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
